subject: ours:discovery
why: Plan 20 D2 fix (critic-34b): check_record.py reads only lines outside code fences and comments, so a fenced example is neither checked, indexed nor continued by --next; it validates the table separator and termination, keeps edge-empty cells, checks every source against its kind's form, accepts any existing prototype: report (code: stays under --root), takes code paths with spaces, and treats a dangling symlink as occupied.

subject: ours:discovery
why: Plan 20 D2 fix (critic-34d, coordinator's decision): check_record.py no longer reads fences or comments. A file is a record only when its first non-blank line is `# Discovery record`, so a commented or fenced example in other notes is neither checked, indexed nor continued by --next; the table ends at its first non-row line (trailing prose passes) and any later line starting with `|` is a problem, whatever surrounds it.

subject: ours:discovery
why: Plan 20 D2 fix (critic-34f N4, coordinator): check_record.py reports any line starting with `|` before the table header, so a malformed earlier table or orphan row can no longer pass unexamined.
